BP/blocks/examples/creative_tanks/example_creative_coolant_tank.json { "format_version": "1.20.80", "minecraft:block": { "description": { "identifier": "utilitycraft:example_creative_coolant_tank", "menu_category": { "category": "construction" } }, "components": { "utilitycraft:infinite_tank": { "resource": "fluid", "type": "example_coolant" }, "minecraft:geometry": "geometry.utilitycraft_creative_fluid_tank", "tag:dorios:fluid": {} } } } Parameter Accepted value Meaning resource "fluid" or "gas" Selects FluidStorage or GasStorage. type non-empty resource type Fixed storage type without namespace, such as example_coolant. Use geometry.utilitycraft_creative_fluid_tank plus a fluid material instance for liquids. Use geometry.utilitycraft_creative_gas_tank, the gas material instance, and the four cardinal rotation permutations from the template for gases. The matching tag:dorios:fluid or tag:dorios:gas makes the block discoverable as a resource endpoint.

This creative component spawns a shared generator helper entity, keeps it full, and transfers energy to the adjacent UtilityCore network. { "utilitycraft:infinite_energy_source": { "rate_speed_base": 10000 }, "minecraft:tick": { "interval_range": [4, 4] }, "tag:dorios:energy": {}, "tag:dorios:generator": {}, "tag:dorios:infinite_energy_source": {} } rate_speed_base is the positive maximum transfer per component tick and defaults to 10000. minecraft:tick is required. The three tags identify the energy endpoint, generator behavior, and infinite source. UtilityCore owns the network this component transfers into.

This data-only block component declares which upgrade category can be installed into each helper-entity slot: { "utilitycraft:machine_upgrades": [ { "type": "speed", "slot": 5, "max": 4 }, { "type": "energy", "slot": 6, "max": 4 }, { "type": "batch", "slot": 7, "max": 4 } ] } It works together with the machine.upgrades slot list, registered upgrade definitions, the upgrade item component, and the UI tab. Follow Register an Upgrade for the complete pipeline.

Reference the UtilityCraft-owned component ID; do not register it again. Copy all required states, traits, ticks, tags, geometries, and permutations from the matching current template example. Keep addon identifiers and textures unique. Confirm UtilityCraft, your BP, UtilityCraft's RP, and your RP are all active. Test placement, breaking, reloading, empty-hand interaction, and adjacent transfer. Continue with Item components.
UtilityCraft reads parameters stored on custom item components. Your addon defines the item and attaches the existing component ID; UtilityCraft registers the behavior once.

A Hammer converts a mined block through the Crusher recipe table. Its tier must meet the recipe's optional tier requirement. BP/items/examples/example_hammer.json { "format_version": "1.21.110", "minecraft:item": { "description": { "identifier": "utilitycraft:example_hammer", "menu_category": { "category": "equipment" } }, "components": { "utilitycraft:hammer": { "tier": 2 }, "minecraft:icon": "utilitycraft_diamond_hammer", "minecraft:max_stack_size": 1, "minecraft:hand_equipped": true, "minecraft:durability": { "max_durability": 512 }, "minecraft:damage": 5, "minecraft:tags": { "tags": [ "minecraft:is_pickaxe", "minecraft:is_tool", "utilitycraft:is_hammer" ] } } } } Parameter Type Meaning tier finite number Minimum recipe tier the tool can process. A tier 2 Hammer can process recipes requiring 0, 1, or 2. The handler looks up the exact mined block in the Crusher registry, removes its normal matching drop, and spawns the registered result and amount. Add a Crusher recipe through Add recipes to existing machines. Durability, mining speed, damage, tags, icon, and recipe are ordinary item configuration owned by the addon; they are not supplied by the custom component.

A Mesh controls Auto Sieve tier, success chance, and output amount: BP/items/examples/example_mesh.json { "format_version": "1.21.110", "minecraft:item": { "description": { "identifier": "utilitycraft:example_mesh", "menu_category": { "category": "construction" } }, "components": { "utilitycraft:mesh": { "tier": 4, "multiplier": 1.5, "amount_multiplier": 1 }, "minecraft:icon": "utilitycraft_diamond_mesh", "minecraft:max_stack_size": 1, "minecraft:durability": { "max_durability": 768 } } } } Parameter Meaning tier Minimum-tier gate for registered Sieve drops. multiplier Multiplies every eligible drop's base chance. 1.5 turns 0.08 into 0.12. amount_multiplier Multiplies the rolled output amount before it is rounded to a whole item. Default behavior is 1. Manual Sieve limitation The current Basic manual Sieve accepts only UtilityCraft's built-in Mesh item IDs. An addon-owned Mesh such as utilitycraft:example_mesh is intended for the Auto Sieve and is deliberately rejected by the manual Sieve interaction handler. Register loot through Fishing and sieve drops.

The Auto Fisher reads all of its equipment modifiers from the installed Fishing Net: BP/items/examples/example_fishing_net.json { "format_version": "1.21.110", "minecraft:item": { "description": { "identifier": "utilitycraft:example_fishing_net", "menu_category": { "category": "construction" } }, "components": { "utilitycraft:fishing_net": { "tier": 4, "speed": 1.5, "chance_multiplier": 1.75, "amount_multiplier": 1, "rolls": 2, "luck": 3 }, "minecraft:icon": "utilitycraft_diamond_fishing_net", "minecraft:max_stack_size": 1, "minecraft:durability": { "max_durability": 768 } } } } Parameter Default Meaning tier 0 Minimum-tier gate for loot entries. speed 1 Multiplies the Auto Fisher processing rate. chance_multiplier 1 Multiplies each eligible base drop chance. amount_multiplier 1 Multiplies rolled item amounts. rolls 1 Loot rolls performed for each completed process. luck 0 Improves supported enchantment chances, counts, and quality for built-in enchantable loot. Use positive, intentionally balanced values. Increasing both rolls and chance_multiplier compounds output much faster than changing either one alone.

Attach this behavior to every item installed through UtilityCraft's upgrade interaction: { "utilitycraft:machine_upgrade": {}, "minecraft:max_stack_size": 4, "minecraft:tags": { "tags": ["utilitycraft:is_upgrade"] } } The component handles using the item on a compatible machine. Its perk type and level values come from DoriosLib.registry.registerMachineUpgrade(), while the machine's block component declares the accepted slot and maximum level. Follow Machine Upgrades instead of configuring these pieces independently.

Item Minimum test Hammer Mine a block with a registered Crusher recipe below and above the Hammer tier. Mesh Install it in an Auto Sieve, test a guaranteed drop, then restore the intended probability. Fishing Net Install it in an Auto Fisher near water and compare rate, eligible tier, and rolls. Upgrade Use and sneak-use it on a compatible machine; verify the correct slot, level cap, and perk. Do not register any of these component IDs again. To create genuinely different behavior, define an addon-owned ID and handler with DoriosLib.registry.itemComponent(). Continue with Generators.

UtilityCraft/RP/ui/ui_core.json is the shared JSON UI control library used by UtilityCraft machinery and compatible extensions. It defines the uc namespace and supplies screens, labels, slots, progress displays, resource bars, upgrade tabs, IO configuration, information tabs, toggles, and lower-level helpers. Do not copy ui_core.json into your addon UtilityCraft already loads this file from its Resource Pack. Your addon only creates and registers its own UI files, then references the shared elements with @uc.<element>. Duplicating the namespace creates version conflicts and prevents UtilityCraft from updating the shared UI safely. Dependency contract: the UtilityCraft Resource Pack must be active below or alongside the extension according to the world pack stack. The extension does not bundle another copy of UI Core or its textures.

This is a production UtilityCraft Assembler screen. The title, gray machine screen, energy bar, slot outlines, upgrades, IO tab, and information tab are composed from uc controls. The texture previews throughout this section are copied into the documentation site only from UtilityCraft's real RP assets. They show the actual pixels used in-game; they are not files an addon should duplicate.
documents.s: What the shared controls look like

documents.t: Your Resource Pack lists its own file: RP/ui/_ui_defs.json { "ui_defs": [ "ui/example_machinery.json" ] } Then the addon-owned UI uses a different namespace and references UtilityCraft controls: RP/ui/example_machinery.json { "namespace": "example_ui", "crusher_top": { "type": "collection_panel", "anchor_from": "center", "anchor_to": "center", "size": [162, 72], "offset": [-10, -40], "collection_name": "container_items", "$item_collection_name": "container_items", "controls": [ { "machine_name@uc.machine_name": {} }, { "screen@uc.machine_small_screen": {} }, { "description@uc.text_label": { "collection_index": 1, "offset": [14, 12], "size": [48, 48], "$text_scale": 0.55 } }, { "energy@uc.energy_bar": { "offset": [-101, -13] } }, { "input@uc.input_slot": { "collection_index": 3, "offset": [0, 30] } }, { "progress@uc.progress_display": { "collection_index": 2, "offset": [28, 23] } }, { "output@uc.output_slot": { "collection_index": 4, "offset": [56, 26] } }, { "upgrades@uc.upgrades_tab": {} }, { "io@uc.io_tab": {} }, { "info@uc.info_tab": { "$info_description": "ui.example:info.crusher" } } ] } } The complete UtilityCraft Addon Template includes the chest-screen routing, labels, entities, and container indices required for a working machine.

{ "local_control_name@uc.shared_element": { "collection_index": 4, "offset": [20, 24], "$custom_variable": "value" } } Part Meaning local_control_name Name unique inside the current controls array. It does not need to match the shared name. @uc.shared_element Inherits the named control from UtilityCraft's uc namespace. $custom_variable Parameter intentionally exposed by that shared element. collection_index Index in the helper entity's container_items collection. It is a standard JSON UI property, not a UI Core $ variable. anchor_from, anchor_to, offset, size, layer, visible Standard JSON UI overrides accepted where appropriate by the inherited control. The reference tables list custom $variables. Standard JSON UI properties are not repeated in every row.

UI Core does not decide which machine value belongs in an inventory slot. The machine helper entity, labels, button items, progress frames, resource display items, and IO buttons must be written to the same indices referenced by the JSON UI. For example: Index Typical content Control 1 Machine information label uc.text_label 2 Progress frame item uc.progress_display 3 Input item uc.input_slot 4 Output item uc.output_slot 5–8 Upgrade items uc.upgrades_tab variables 9+ IO face button items uc.io_tab direction-index variables The actual indices are machine-owned. Override every relevant variable when your entity layout differs from a control's defaults.

Category Contents Visibility, labels, tooltips, and buttons Conditional panels, hover text, machine title, dynamic labels, slot hover behavior, and buttons. Items and slots Item renderers, progress displays, input/output/fuel/upgrade slots, and the numbered IO outline families. Bars, grids, and screens Energy/liquid bars, multi-bars, slot layouts, machine screens, and side panels. Tabs and IO configuration Generic toggles, upgrade tab, IO face controls, IO tab, and information tab. Complete element index All 100 top-level definitions, inheritance relationships, and public status.

Names beginning with _, such as uc._slot_visual, are implementation primitives used to build stable public controls. They remain listed because they exist in ui_core.json, but normal extension UIs should prefer their public wrappers. Controls inheriting @common.* or other uc elements are templates, not separate files that must be registered.

Resource bars visualize display items supplied by the helper entity. Energy, liquid, and gas storage classes are responsible for selecting and updating those display items; the JSON UI control supplies the border, tooltip, and placement.
documents.s: Resource bars, slot layouts, and screens

documents.t: Element Capacity display Border Variables uc.energy_bar One large display item Energy $item_collection_name, $has_bg, $bar_bg_texture, $collection_index uc.fluid_bar One large display item Liquid $item_collection_name, $has_bg, $collection_index uc.liquid_bar One large display item Liquid plus optional IO outline $item_collection_name, $has_bg, $bar_bg_texture, $collection_index, $show_liquid_outline, $liquid_outline_texture uc.big_energy_bar Three overlapping display items Wide energy $item_collection_name, $collection_index uc.big_fluid_bar Three overlapping display items Wide liquid $item_collection_name, $collection_index Defaults are container_items, index 0, and no background except for energy_bar, whose $has_bg is true. The default $bar_bg_texture is textures/ui/toggle_button/left_bg. liquid_bar defaults $show_liquid_outline to false and $liquid_outline_texture to the input-1 outline. Energy and liquid displays { "energy@uc.energy_bar": { "$collection_index": 0, "offset": [-101, -13] } }, { "coolant@uc.liquid_input_1_bar": { "$collection_index": 6, "offset": [-80, -13] } } $collection_index versus collection_index The resource-bar wrappers expose $collection_index and forward it to their nested display. Slot controls usually receive the standard collection_index property directly. Follow the variable table for the selected control. energy_bar border liquid_bar border big_energy_bar border big_fluid_bar border

The following controls inherit uc.liquid_bar, enable its IO outline, and choose an exact IO color. They accept the same variables as liquid_bar; overriding $liquid_outline_texture is possible but normally unnecessary. Direction Exact controls Inputs uc.liquid_input_1_bar through uc.liquid_input_9_bar Outputs uc.liquid_output_1_bar through uc.liquid_output_9_bar Fuel uc.liquid_fuel_bar Use the alias matching the port type registered by the machine. The number is meaningful: it connects the display color to the same input_1 through input_9 or output_1 through output_9 IO types used by DoriosCore.

These lower-level wrappers are useful when a custom display spans several item frames. Element Visible parts Variables uc.bar 1 $item_collection_name, $is_energy, $is_liquid, $has_bg, $bar_bg_texture, $collection_index uc.bar_double 2 $item_collection_name, $is_energy, $is_liquid, $collection_index uc.bar_triple 3 Same uc.bar_quadruple 4 Same uc.bar_quintuple 5 Same $is_energy and $is_liquid default to false; enable only the border that represents the resource. All parts use the same collection index because a storage display is composed from overlapping render passes of the same display item.

Internal implementation for two- through five-part bars. It accepts: Variable Default Purpose $item_collection_name "container_items" Source collection. $is_energy, $is_liquid false Selects the wide border. $collection_index 0 Display-item index. $show_1, $show_2, $show_3 true Shows the first three render parts. $show_4, $show_5 false Shows the optional fourth and fifth parts. $offset_1 ... $offset_5 [-6,14], [10,14], [26,14], [42,14], [58,14] Position of each render part. uc.bar_background draws the optional background. It accepts $bar_bg_texture (default textures/ui/toggle_button/left_bg); its nested cell size is fixed to [24, 56].

Places up to three native container items vertically. It accepts: Variable Default $item_collection_name "container_items" $has_bg false $has_first, $has_second, $has_third true $collection_index_first 0 $collection_index_second 1 $collection_index_third 2

Uses the same visibility and index variables, without $has_bg, and positions the items left, center, and right. { "inputs@uc.slot_stack_horizontal": { "$collection_index_first": 3, "$collection_index_second": 4, "$collection_index_third": 5, "$has_third": false, "offset": [-18, 0] } }

Element Size Indices Variables uc.slot_grid_2x2 36x36 $collection_index_1 ... $collection_index_4, default 0 ... 3 $item_collection_name, $slot_outline_texture, index variables uc.slot_grid_3x3 54x54 $collection_index_1 ... $collection_index_9, default 0 ... 8 Same family through index 9 $slot_outline_texture defaults to textures/ui/slots/default_slot. The grid outline is 38x38 for the 2x2 control and 56x56 for the 3x3 control, extending one pixel around the interactive cells. { "recipe_inputs@uc.slot_grid_3x3": { "offset": [12, 13], "$collection_index_1": 3, "$collection_index_2": 4, "$collection_index_3": 5, "$collection_index_4": 6, "$collection_index_5": 7, "$collection_index_6": 8, "$collection_index_7": 9, "$collection_index_8": 10, "$collection_index_9": 11, "$slot_outline_texture": "textures/ui/slots/input_1_slot" } }

Element Size Default offset Purpose uc.machine_small_screen 52x52 [11, 14] Standard square machine content area. uc.big_machine_screen 104x52 [11, 14] Wide content area for a larger slot layout or additional status. uc.machine_side_panel 90x166 [-86, -7] Extra panel to the left of the standard machine window. machine_small_screen big_machine_screen machine_side_panel The side panel accepts $item_collection_name, defaulting to container_items. Use it only when the standard machine screen cannot contain the required controls. For a normal machine whose controls fit, keep the standard screen and machine label arrangement used by UtilityCraft.

This index contains every top-level definition currently exported by UtilityCraft/RP/ui/ui_core.json: 100 controls in the uc namespace. Reference a control as local_name@uc.element_name from an addon-owned UI file. Status meanings: Public: intended for normal machine UI composition. Alias: public preset inheriting another UI Core control. Low-level: compositional control used by a larger public control; use it only for a custom UI abstraction. Internal: implementation primitive beginning with _; prefer its public wrapper.

All controls are referenced from an addon-owned UI file with @uc.<name>.

Element Variables What it does uc.function_panel None Reads #item_id_aux from container_items and is visible while the bound numeric item ID is below 1. Used for an empty/absent-state overlay. uc.second_function_panel None Inverse of function_panel; visible when the numeric item ID is 1 or greater. uc.hover_text_function_panel $function_item_name required Visible when #hover_text does not contain the supplied function marker. uc.second_hover_text_function_panel $function_item_name required Inverse hover-text condition; visible when the marker is present. These are binding templates. Set collection_index on the inherited instance so the collection binding reads the intended helper-entity slot. { "empty_overlay@uc.function_panel": { "collection_index": 3, "controls": [ { "ghost": { "type": "image", "texture": "textures/items/example_input_ghost", "alpha": 0.5 } } ] } }

Draws a purple tooltip-style image with a localized label. Variable Type Default Purpose $hover_text string "" Text or localization key shown in the tooltip. The control is anchored at the top-left, offset [23, 2], placed at layer 80, and does not clip its content.

An invisible 16×16 button whose hover state creates uc.fake_hover_text. Variable Type Default $hover_text string "" Use it when a normal JSON UI control needs a tooltip but is not itself a container slot.

Element Variables Purpose uc.slot_button_prototype None Extends common.container_slot_button_prototype and maps mouse, controller, auto-place, and inventory-drop inputs to button.container_auto_place. uc.slot_button $highlight_control = "uc.slot_highlight" Button wrapper that displays the selected highlight control on hover. uc.slot_highlight None Uses common.hover_text bound to the current item collection's #hover_text. Change $highlight_control only when providing a compatible control reference with the same hover responsibilities.

Reads text from the instance's collection_index, anchors it top-left, and renders it with the current label compatibility logic. Variable Type Default Purpose $text_scale number 1 font_scale_factor for both internal label variants. { "description@uc.text_label": { "collection_index": 1, "anchor_from": "top_left", "anchor_to": "top_left", "offset": [14, 12], "size": [48, 48], "$text_scale": 0.55 } }
Same data source and $text_scale, but uses a 52×52 panel with a centered 48-pixel-wide text area.

Internal label implementations used by both wrappers. Element Bound text Behavior _text_label_v1 #hover_text Direct collection binding. _text_label_v2 #displaying_text Visibility-change binding that remains visible only while the always-bound and displayed text agree or the always-bound text is empty. Both accept $text_scale with default 1. Prefer text_label or centered_text_label rather than referencing these primitives directly.

Wraps chest.chest_label, which displays the current container title. Variable Type Default Purpose $offset [number, number] [10, 0] Title offset inside the machine panel. { "machine_name@uc.machine_name": {} } The visible text comes from the helper entity/container title and its language entry; it is not passed as a UI variable.

A collection_panel that sends button.drop_all when pressed. DoriosCore/DoriosLib interface logic interprets the helper item and button action. Variable Type Default $item_collection_name string "container_items" $button_size [number, number] [18, 18] $button_text string " " $text_scale number 1 $default_texture texture path textures/ui/buttons/power_button $hover_texture texture path textures/ui/buttons/power_button_selected $pressed_texture texture path textures/ui/buttons/power_button_pressed

Uses the same collection, size, scale, texture variables, mappings, and click sound. Instead of $button_text, its label is bound to the selected collection item's #hover_text. { "increase@uc.machine_button": { "collection_index": 4, "$button_size": [24, 16], "$button_text": "+1", "$text_scale": 0.6, "$default_texture": "textures/ui/buttons/button", "$hover_texture": "textures/ui/buttons/button_selected", "$pressed_texture": "textures/ui/buttons/button_pressed" } } default hover pressed
An empty collection_panel template sized to its children. It accepts $item_collection_name, defaulting to container_items, and is useful as a collection-bound base for addon-owned slot compositions.

These controls render items already present in the machine helper entity's container_items collection. They do not create an inventory, move items, or choose an IO mode. The script and entity definition own that behavior; JSON UI only displays the corresponding collection index.

Element Cell / renderer size Hover Intended use uc.button_item_display 18 / 16 Button behavior Small collection-backed button icon. uc.item_display 18 / 16 No Small read-only item or state frame. uc.item_display_medium 34 / 32 No Medium read-only item. uc.item_display_large 50 / 48 No Large read-only resource fill or illustration. uc.item_display_hover 18 / 16 Yes Small item with item tooltip and focus navigation. uc.item_display_hover_medium 34 / 32 Yes Medium item with tooltip. uc.item_display_hover_large 50 / 48 Yes Large item with tooltip; used by resource bars. uc.progress_display 34 / 32 No Animated progress-frame item. Focus navigation is disabled. uc.output_item 26 / 26 Native slot Large output item primitive. uc.input_item 18 / 18 Native slot Standard container item primitive. Display a script-updated progress frame { "progress@uc.progress_display": { "collection_index": 2, "offset": [28, 23] } } progress_display does not calculate progress. The machine script updates the item at index 2 to the correct frame identifier, and the UI renders that item.

The display controls expose the variables below. A wrapper may fix some values to its documented size. Variable Type Default Purpose $cell_image_size [number, number] Depends on control Overall cell image size. $cell_overlay_ref control reference "common.cell_overlay" Overlay used for stack count, durability, and storage indicators. $stack_count_required boolean true Enables the stack-count overlay. $durability_bar_required boolean true Enables the durability overlay when applicable. $storage_bar_required boolean true Enables the storage overlay when applicable. $item_renderer control reference "common.item_renderer" Minecraft item-renderer control. $item_renderer_panel_size [number, number] Depends on control Panel containing the rendered item. $item_renderer_size [number, number] Depends on control Rendered item size. $item_renderer_offset [number, number] [0, 0] Item offset inside its renderer panel. Hover variants additionally accept: Variable Type Default Purpose $button_ref control reference "uc.slot_button" Button/tooltip implementation placed over the item. $focus_id string "" Controller focus identifier. $focus_override_up string "" Explicit focus destination when moving up. $focus_override_down string "" Explicit focus destination when moving down. $focus_override_left string "" Explicit focus destination when moving left. $focus_override_right string "" Explicit focus destination when moving right.

uc._slot_visual and uc._slot_visual_hover implement the renderer, overlay, count, durability/storage bars, and focus bindings used by the public controls. _slot_visual_hover also accepts $button_ref. Their remaining variables are the common item-renderer and focus variables listed above. Prefer a public item_display* wrapper unless you are building a new shared UI abstraction and need full control over the renderer internals.

Element Size Variables What it displays uc.input_slot 18x18 $slot_background_texture = textures/ui/slots/input_1_slot Interactive container item with an input outline. uc.fuel_slot 18x18 None Interactive container item with the fuel outline. uc.upgrade_slot 18x18 $show_slot_background = true Interactive upgrade slot; its outline can be hidden. uc.output_slot 26x26 $slot_background_texture = textures/ui/slots/output_1_slot Larger interactive container item with an output outline. Input, progress, and output { "input@uc.input_slot": { "collection_index": 3, "offset": [0, 30] } }, { "progress@uc.progress_display": { "collection_index": 2, "offset": [28, 23] } }, { "output@uc.output_slot": { "collection_index": 4, "offset": [56, 26] } } Slot names are exact The recognized numbered controls are input_1_slot through input_9_slot and output_1_slot through output_9_slot. Names such as input_1, input_2, or output_1 are not UI Core controls.

uc.input_1_slot through uc.input_9_slot inherit uc.input_slot and set the matching outline texture. Use the number assigned by the machine's IO definition. { "secondary_input@uc.input_2_slot": { "collection_index": 4, "offset": [18, 30] } } input_1_slot input_2_slot input_3_slot input_4_slot input_5_slot input_6_slot input_7_slot input_8_slot input_9_slot

uc.output_1_slot through uc.output_9_slot inherit uc.output_slot and select the matching output outline. output_1_slot output_2_slot output_3_slot output_4_slot output_5_slot output_6_slot output_7_slot output_8_slot output_9_slot

These textures are also consumed by uc.io_face_outline to explain the state encoded by an IO button item. default disabled / none normal both upgrade fuel item resource liquid resource gas resource energy

The standard right-side machine tabs share one radio-toggle group. Opening upgrades, IO, or information selects that tab; selecting the close state hides the active panel. Keep the default shared group names unless you intentionally build more than one independent tab set in the same screen. upgrades closed upgrades open IO closed IO open info closed info open

{ "upgrades@uc.upgrades_tab": { "$upgrade_index_1": 5, "$upgrade_index_2": 6, "$has_first_upgrade": true, "$has_second_upgrade": true } }, { "io@uc.io_tab": { "$has_item_io": true, "$has_fluid_io": true, "$has_gas_io": false, "$io_item_top_index": 8, "$io_fluid_top_index": 14 } }, { "info@uc.info_tab": { "$info_description": "ui.example:info.machine" } } All three controls default $item_collection_name to container_items. upgrades_tab, io_tab, and info_tab also default $right_machine_tabs_name to right_machine_tabs, which makes them mutually exclusive.

Creates the standard upgrades button and panel. The panel supports up to four upgrade slots. Variable Type Default Purpose $item_collection_name string "container_items" Collection containing upgrade items. $upgrade_index_1 ... $upgrade_index_4 number 4, 5, 6, 7 Collection index for each upgrade slot. $has_first_upgrade boolean true Shows slot 1. $has_second_upgrade boolean true Shows slot 2. $has_third_upgrade boolean false Shows slot 3. $has_fourth_upgrade boolean false Shows slot 4. $upgrade_overlay_1 texture path textures/items/machinery/speed_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 1. $upgrade_overlay_2 texture path textures/items/machinery/energy_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 2. $upgrade_overlay_3 texture path textures/items/machinery/range_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 3. $upgrade_overlay_4 texture path textures/items/machinery/quantity_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 4. $right_machine_tabs_name string "right_machine_tabs" Shared radio-toggle group. $upgrade_toggle_control_name string "upgrade_toggle_button" Binding name used to open and close the panel. The UI overlays are visual hints only. The machine's registered upgrade slots and upgrade definitions determine which items are accepted and which values are modified.

Creates the standard IO button and configuration panel. It can expose separate item, liquid, and gas pages. Each page contains six block-face buttons in this order: top, left, front, right, bottom, back.

Variable Type Default Purpose $item_collection_name string "container_items" Collection containing IO button items. $info_description string "" Reserved description value passed by the shared panel. $has_io_config boolean true Shows the IO configuration feature. $has_item_io boolean true Shows the item page selector and face controls. $has_fluid_io boolean false Shows the liquid page selector and face controls. $has_gas_io boolean false Shows the gas page selector and face controls. $io_items_default boolean true Initial checked state for the item selector. $io_fluids_default boolean false Initial checked state for the liquid selector. $io_gases_default boolean false Initial checked state for the gas selector. $io_default_tab_index number 0 Forced selected index in the item/liquid/gas radio group. $right_machine_tabs_name string "right_machine_tabs" Shared right-side tab group. $io_toggle_control_name string "io_toggle_button" Open/close binding name. $io_config_tabs_name string "io_config_tabs" Item/liquid/gas radio group name. $io_items_toggle_control_name string "io_items_toggle_button" Item-page binding name. $io_fluids_toggle_control_name string "io_fluids_toggle_button" Liquid-page binding name. $io_gases_toggle_control_name string "io_gases_toggle_button" Gas-page binding name. The three default mode descriptions are IO Modes: followed by blue inputs 1-9 and red outputs 1-9. Override them when a machine supports fewer modes or additional semantic roles: { "io@uc.io_tab": { "$has_item_io": true, "$has_fluid_io": true, "$io_items_modes_description": "§rItem IO Modes:
§r- §9Input 1
§r- §cOutput 1", "$io_fluids_modes_description": "§rLiquid IO Modes:
§r- §9Input 1" } } Use §r at the beginning of every custom formatted line so formatting inherited from another label or item name cannot leak into it.

Resource Top Left Front Right Bottom Back Item $io_item_top_index = 8 $io_item_left_index = 9 $io_item_front_index = 10 $io_item_right_index = 11 $io_item_bottom_index = 12 $io_item_back_index = 13 Liquid $io_fluid_top_index = 14 $io_fluid_left_index = 15 $io_fluid_front_index = 16 $io_fluid_right_index = 17 $io_fluid_bottom_index = 18 $io_fluid_back_index = 19 Gas $io_gas_top_index = 20 $io_gas_left_index = 21 $io_gas_front_index = 22 $io_gas_right_index = 23 $io_gas_bottom_index = 24 $io_gas_back_index = 25 Every visible resource page needs six valid helper-entity indices. The item at each index carries the current IO state in its hover text; clicking the face button dispatches the shared machine-button action.

Variable Default texture $io_top_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_up $io_left_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_west $io_front_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_north $io_right_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_east $io_bottom_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_down $io_back_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_south These six textures visualize block orientation. Override them only when the machine needs a different face diagram. items unchecked items checked liquids unchecked liquids checked gases unchecked gases checked
Normal machines should use uc.io_tab. The following controls are its compositional parts.

Builds the six-face diagram. It accepts $io_top_index, $io_left_index, $io_front_index, $io_right_index, $io_bottom_index, and $io_back_index (defaults 8-13), plus the six $io_*_texture variables listed above.

Combines one machine button, one face texture, and one state outline. Variable Default $item_collection_name "container_items" $io_button_index 0 $io_button_offset [0, 0] $io_face_offset [0, 1] $io_face_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_north

Reads the selected IO button item's hover text and draws the outline matching its exact state marker. Variable family Defaults / accepted states $item_collection_name, $io_button_index, $io_button_offset container_items, 0, [0,0] $io_default_texture, $io_disabled_texture, $io_none_texture, $io_normal_texture Corresponding default, none, and normal slot textures. $io_input_1_texture ... $io_input_9_texture textures/ui/slots/input_1_slot ... input_9_slot. $io_output_1_texture ... $io_output_9_texture textures/ui/slots/output_1_slot ... output_9_slot. $io_both_texture, $io_upgrade_texture, $io_fuel_texture Corresponding slot textures. $io_item_resource_texture, $io_liquid_resource_texture, $io_gas_resource_texture, $io_energy_texture Corresponding resource slot textures. The exact recognized state markers are default, disabled, none, normal, input_1 through input_9, output_1 through output_9, both, upgrade, fuel, item_resource, liquid_resource, gas_resource, and energy. uc.io_state_outline is the internal 18x18 image primitive used once per possible state. It expects $item_collection_name, $io_button_index, $io_button_offset, $io_state_name, and $io_outline_texture from its parent.

Creates a localized, scrollable information panel. Variable Type Default Purpose $item_collection_name string "container_items" Shared collection context. $info_description string "" when omitted Localization key or literal description shown in the scroll area. $right_machine_tabs_name string "right_machine_tabs" Shared right-tab radio group. $info_toggle_control_name string "info_toggle_button" Open/close binding name. uc.info_description_scroll_content is the internal vertical scrolling content. It accepts $info_description, default "". For a normal machine, pass the value to info_tab and let it compose the scroll control.

A reusable Minecraft JSON UI toggle with optional radio grouping, tooltip, background, and icon. Variable group Variables and defaults Identity/state $toggle_name="toggle_button", $toggle_index=0, $toggle_group=false, $toggle_default_state=false, $toggle_group_default_selected=0, $toggle_control_name="" Layout $toggle_layer=0, $toggle_size=[18,18], $toggle_lost_reset=true Tooltip $toggle_hover_text="", $toggle_checked_hover_text="", both localization flags false, $toggle_checked_hover_text_from_hover=false State textures $toggle_unchecked, $toggle_checked, $toggle_unchecked_hover, $toggle_checked_hover use the matching textures/ui/buttons/* defaults Background $has_toggle_bg=false, $toggle_bg_texture="textures/ui/toggle_button/right_bg", $toggle_bg_size=[24,24], $toggle_bg_offset=[0,0], $toggle_bg_layer=-6 Optional icon $has_toggle_icon=false, $toggle_icon_size=[16,16], four $toggle_icon_* texture paths default to "", $toggle_icon_uv_size=[16,16] uc.button_display renders the collection item used as a 16x16 button visual. It accepts $item_collection_name and $collection_index (default 0). uc.toggle_button_panel shows an arbitrary $controls array while the toggle named by $panel_control_name is checked. Both variables default to an empty value.

Estúdio Bedrock independente · Desde 2022 Equipe pequena. Mundos maiores. A Dorios Studios é um coletivo de criadores que desenvolve addons gratuitos para Minecraft Bedrock, com sistemas úteis, progressão bem pensada e uma comunidade que continua moldando o trabalho. Conheça a equipe Explore os projetos Fundação 09.09.2022 Plataforma Minecraft Bedrock Foco Addons gratuitos feitos para jogadores Por que existimos Criar mais possibilidades em cada mundo. Acreditamos que jogadores de Bedrock merecem experiências ambiciosas e de alta qualidade sem que as ideias mais interessantes fiquem atrás de uma cobrança. Nosso trabalho vai da automação industrial à exploração e mecânicas personalizadas, sempre com o mesmo padrão: acessível no começo, recompensador como sistema e bom de compartilhar. Nossa história Construída por iteração. De experimentos individuais a um coletivo multidisciplinar de Bedrock. 2020 Os primeiros experimentos Milo504 começou a criar addons de Bedrock com More Armors, seguido por Tools, Weapons and More — o projeto que mais tarde se tornaria UtilityCraft. 2022 A Dorios Studios ganha forma Milo504 e WeatherVictor fundaram a Dorios Studios em 9 de setembro, reunindo desenvolvimento e design de interfaces sob uma identidade comum. 2024 Uma linguagem visual mais clara JR.ice entrou como designer principal e artista de texturas. UtilityCraft 3.0 veio em seguida, tornando-se o primeiro grande marco do estúdio na comunidade Bedrock. Nossa abordagem Princípios que sobrevivem ao protótipo. Abra um princípio para ver como ele orienta o trabalho. 01Bedrock primeiroProjetar para a plataforma que os jogadores realmente usam.+ Controles, multijogador, desempenho e o ecossistema de addons Bedrock orientam cada decisão desde o início; não são uma adaptação feita no final. 02Sistemas com propósitoDar a cada mecânica um lugar na progressão.+ Automação útil, progressão legível e espaço para experimentar transformam recursos isolados em mundos que continuam interessantes amanhã. 03Moldado pela comunidadeTratar o feedback como parte do trabalho.+ Jogadores e testadores ajudam a revelar o que está confuso, desequilibrado ou ainda não está divertido. Esse retorno orienta a evolução dos addons. Dentro do estúdio Pessoas e agradecimentos. A equipe registra quem faz o trabalho. Os créditos registram todas as pessoas e ferramentas que o tornam possível. 01 / Pessoas Equipe Conheça a equipe do estúdio, suas principais áreas e os criadores que colaboram conosco. Ver equipe 02 / Agradecimentos Créditos Colaboradores, testadores, apoio da comunidade e ferramentas de código aberto por trás do site. Ler créditos Comunidade e valores O feedback faz parte do processo. Compartilhe o que funciona, relate o que não funciona e nos ajude a entender o que jogadores de Bedrock querem construir a seguir. Um retorno cuidadoso fortalece cada lançamento. Participe da conversa Apoie o estúdio

Direção Origem → rede → destino Filtro Instale uma Melhoria de Filtro: a lista de permissão aceita os recursos listados; a lista de bloqueio os exclui. Filtro de itens vazio Com filtro instalado, uma lista de permissão vazia bloqueia a exportação; uma lista de bloqueio vazia permite todos os itens. Modos de distribuição Nearest prioriza os destinos mais próximos; Farthest prioriza os mais distantes; Round Robin alterna o próximo destino após uma transferência bem-sucedida. Vazão estimada de itens Exporter: uma operação a cada 10 ticks, até 64 itens por operação; aproximadamente 128 itens/s com pilhas cheias. Quatro Melhorias de Velocidade elevam o limite a cinco operações/ciclo, até 640 itens/s. Vazão de líquidos e gases Limite do Exporter: 4.000 mB por ciclo, multiplicado por 1–5 com Melhorias de Velocidade. Cada recurso usa seu próprio limite de transferência. Configuração de recursos Itens, líquidos e gases são configurados separadamente no menu do terminal. Conexão de energia Também conecta a rede de energia pelas faces habilitadas. Os ajustes de itens, líquidos e gases pertencem aos respectivos sistemas de transferência. Conexões Cores de tubos compatíveis e faces habilitadas precisam ligar a origem aos destinos. Configure as faces com a Chave Inglesa; copie ajustes compatíveis com a ferramenta de copiar e colar. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real.

BlocoOverworldMaquinário Visão geralEspecificaçõesReceitas Funcionamento do transporte Retira recursos do inventário ou tanque de origem conectado e os envia aos destinos compatíveis da rede. Direção Origem → rede → destino Filtro Instale uma Melhoria de Filtro: a lista de permissão aceita os recursos listados; a lista de bloqueio os exclui. Filtro de itens vazio Com filtro instalado, uma lista de permissão vazia bloqueia a exportação; uma lista de bloqueio vazia permite todos os itens. Modos de distribuição Nearest prioriza os destinos mais próximos; Farthest prioriza os mais distantes; Round Robin alterna o próximo destino após uma transferência bem-sucedida. Vazão estimada de itens Exporter: uma operação a cada 10 ticks, até 64 itens por operação; aproximadamente 128 itens/s com pilhas cheias. Quatro Melhorias de Velocidade elevam o limite a cinco operações/ciclo, até 640 itens/s. Vazão de líquidos e gases Limite do Exporter: 4.000 mB por ciclo, multiplicado por 1–5 com Melhorias de Velocidade. Cada recurso usa seu próprio limite de transferência. Configuração de recursos Itens, líquidos e gases são configurados separadamente no menu do terminal. Conexão de energia Também conecta a rede de energia pelas faces habilitadas. Os ajustes de itens, líquidos e gases pertencem aos respectivos sistemas de transferência. Conexões Cores de tubos compatíveis e faces habilitadas precisam ligar a origem aos destinos. Configure as faces com a Chave Inglesa; copie ajustes compatíveis com a ferramenta de copiar e colar. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real. Dorios Energy The shared power network used by Ascendant machines, storage, relays, Power Beacons, and absolute-tier infrastructure. Gas Management The gas input, storage, processing, and output system used by supported superior machines and recipes. Superior Machines Advanced processors with specialized item, liquid, gas, catalyst, and upgrade slots for late-game production. Absolute Generators The fifth generator tier, built to supply high-output Dorios Energy for Ascendant industrial networks. Cryogenic Branches Cryogenic work is split between the Cryo Freezer, Cryofluid Synthesizer, and Cryo Stabilizer so each production lane can scale independently. Overclock Network An Overclock Tower consumes fuel, Reinforced Cable carries the network, and Overclock Relays distribute the selected boost to supported machines. Progression Status Aetherium, Titanium, and Tungsten are documented current materials. Niobium, Singularities, and Kyarium remain planned progression; the Singularity Fabricator is pending rework. End-game architecture Specialized machines, shared industrial core. Ascendant Technology raises infrastructure costs and process complexity while keeping energy, fluids, recipes, and machine state compatible with UtilityCraft.

ProjetosHeavy MachineryHeavy Machinery Wiki Pesquisar nesta seção da wikiCtrl K Mecânicas Pesquisar nesta seção da wikiCtrl KNavegar Heavy Machinery Visão geral Visão geral Conteúdo ItensBlocos Sistemas MáquinasGeradores Referência ReceitasMecânicas Repositório no GitHub Índice de Heavy Machinery Mecânicas 7 sistemas principais The shared systems that make machines, generators, ports, and modules work together. Dorios Energy The UtilityCraft power system used by multiblock controllers, energy ports, storage components, factories, and generators. Fluid Management The liquid input, storage, transfer, and output system used by chambers, reactors, tanks, and multiblock ports. Multiblock Machines Expandable processing factories assembled from one controller, compatible casings, ports, and internal modules. Multiblock Generators Large structures that generate, buffer, and distribute Dorios Energy through configurable internal components. Uranium Fuel Cycle Raw uranium is processed into uranium products, converted into uranium hexafluoride, enriched in the Isotope Centrifuge, formed into Enriched Uranium Fuel Rods, and consumed by the Nuclear Reactor while producing waste gas. Hazard Equipment Hazmat pieces carry the shared hazard-equipment tag and offer repairable armor protection. Utility Exo pieces provide extremely durable wearable equipment; special abilities are documented only when implemented. Modular Storage Liquid and Gas Tank Controllers form steel-cased storage structures with five independent channels. Cells add capacity and compatible ports provide per-face automation. Construction rule One controller. One valid shell. Your choice of internals. The controller indexes every compatible component inside the detected structure. This makes size and module distribution part of the machine design rather than a fixed recipe.

BlocoOverworldMaquinário Visão geralEspecificaçõesReceitas Identificador utilitycraft:ender_hopper Block type Bloco Nível Maquinário Break time 1 s Funcionamento do transporte Coleta itens soltos próximos e os envia ao inventário abaixo. Filtro Uma Melhoria de Filtro habilita uma lista de permissão ou bloqueio por tipo de item. O filtro vale para coleta e saída. Velocidade estimada Um ciclo a cada 8 ticks (cerca de 2,5 ciclos/s). Cada etapa de coleta/saída tenta mover 1–5 pilhas com 0–4 Melhorias de Velocidade: cerca de 2,5–12,5 tentativas de pilha/s por etapa. Distribuição Usa sua direção física de saída. Nearest, Farthest e Round Robin são modos dos Exporters de rede. Raio de coleta Padrão: 3 blocos; cada Melhoria de Alcance adiciona 2 blocos, até 11. O raio de coleta pode ser reduzido no menu. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real.

ProjetosUtilityCraftUtilityCraft Wiki Pesquisar nesta seção da wikiCtrl K Blocos Pesquisar nesta seção da wikiCtrl KNavegar UtilityCraft Visão geral Visão geral Como jogar Conteúdo ItensBlocos Sistemas MáquinasGeradores Referência ReceitasMecânicas Repositório no GitHub ← Voltar para Blocos Bloco registro Exportador de Itens (Padrão) Retira recursos do inventário ou tanque de origem conectado e os envia aos destinos compatíveis da rede. BlocoOverworldMaquinário Visão geralEspecificaçõesReceitas Identificador utilitycraft:item_exporter Block type Bloco Nível Maquinário Break time 1 s Funcionamento do transporte Retira recursos do inventário ou tanque de origem conectado e os envia aos destinos compatíveis da rede. Direção Origem → rede → destino Filtro Instale uma Melhoria de Filtro: a lista de permissão aceita os recursos listados; a lista de bloqueio os exclui. Filtro de itens vazio Com filtro instalado, uma lista de permissão vazia bloqueia a exportação; uma lista de bloqueio vazia permite todos os itens. Modos de distribuição Nearest prioriza os destinos mais próximos; Farthest prioriza os mais distantes; Round Robin alterna o próximo destino após uma transferência bem-sucedida. Vazão estimada de itens Exporter: uma operação a cada 10 ticks, até 64 itens por operação; aproximadamente 128 itens/s com pilhas cheias. Quatro Melhorias de Velocidade elevam o limite a cinco operações/ciclo, até 640 itens/s. Conexões Cores de tubos compatíveis e faces habilitadas precisam ligar a origem aos destinos. Configure as faces com a Chave Inglesa; copie ajustes compatíveis com a ferramenta de copiar e colar. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real.

BlocoOverworldMaquinário Visão geralEspecificaçõesReceitas Funcionamento do transporte Retira recursos do inventário ou tanque de origem conectado e os envia aos destinos compatíveis da rede. Direção Origem → rede → destino Filtro Instale uma Melhoria de Filtro: a lista de permissão aceita os recursos listados; a lista de bloqueio os exclui. Filtro de itens vazio Com filtro instalado, uma lista de permissão vazia bloqueia a exportação; uma lista de bloqueio vazia permite todos os itens. Modos de distribuição Nearest prioriza os destinos mais próximos; Farthest prioriza os mais distantes; Round Robin alterna o próximo destino após uma transferência bem-sucedida. Vazão estimada de itens Exporter: uma operação a cada 10 ticks, até 64 itens por operação; aproximadamente 128 itens/s com pilhas cheias. Quatro Melhorias de Velocidade elevam o limite a cinco operações/ciclo, até 640 itens/s. Conexões Cores de tubos compatíveis e faces habilitadas precisam ligar a origem aos destinos. Configure as faces com a Chave Inglesa; copie ajustes compatíveis com a ferramenta de copiar e colar. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real. O Exporter executa a transferência. BlocoOverworldMaquinário Visão geralEspecificaçõesReceitas Funcionamento do transporte Recebe os recursos da rede no inventário ou tanque de destino conectado. O Exporter executa a transferência. Direção Rede → destino conectado Filtro Instale uma Melhoria de Filtro: a lista de permissão aceita os recursos listados; a lista de bloqueio os exclui. Filtro de itens vazio Uma lista de itens vazia no Importer aceita todos os itens. O filtro do Exporter de origem continua valendo. Modos de distribuição A ordem dos destinos é escolhida no Exporter de origem: Nearest, Farthest ou Round Robin. Vazão estimada de itens Exporter: uma operação a cada 10 ticks, até 64 itens por operação; aproximadamente 128 itens/s com pilhas cheias. Quatro Melhorias de Velocidade elevam o limite a cinco operações/ciclo, até 640 itens/s. Conexões Cores de tubos compatíveis e faces habilitadas precisam ligar a origem aos destinos. Configure as faces com a Chave Inglesa; copie ajustes compatíveis com a ferramenta de copiar e colar. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real. BlocoOverworldMaquinário Visão geralEspecificaçõesReceitas Identificador utilitycraft:mechanic_dropper Block type Bloco Nível Maquinário Break time 1 s Funcionamento do transporte Retira itens da origem vertical adjacente e ejeta pilhas inteiras no mundo pelo lado oposto. Filtro Uma Melhoria de Filtro habilita uma lista de permissão ou bloqueio por tipo de item. O filtro vale para coleta e saída. Velocidade estimada Um ciclo a cada 8 ticks (cerca de 2,5 ciclos/s). Cada etapa de coleta/saída tenta mover 1–5 pilhas com 0–4 Melhorias de Velocidade: cerca de 2,5–12,5 tentativas de pilha/s por etapa. Distribuição Usa sua direção física de saída. Nearest, Farthest e Round Robin são modos dos Exporters de rede. Estimativas nominais consideram 20 ticks de jogo/s. Tamanho das pilhas, filtros, itens disponíveis, espaço livre, entrada e saída por face e chunks carregados podem reduzir a vazão real.

UtilityCraft reshapes survival from the first day onward: start with simple tools and renewable resources, then grow into powered machines, storage, transport, and full automation. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 Resources, tools and utility Begin with hammers, pebbles, sieves, and mesh progression. Those early loops become a reliable source of ores, seeds, and building materials. Crops, tools, cobblestone generators, and utility blocks reduce repetitive work while keeping the survival progression intact. 02 Machines and energy Machines, generators, batteries, and upgrades form the heart of UtilityCraft automation. Process items, route Dorios Energy, and scale a small workshop into a factory. Liquid tanks and mob-grinding systems extend the same production network with fluid storage, automated drops, and experience handling. 03 Your progression path 01 Gather pebbles and loose materials with a Wooden or Stone Hammer. 02 Craft a Flint Knife, String Mesh, and Sieve to unlock renewable resources. 03 Scale sieving, produce Water and Lava, then prepare Steel. 04 Craft the UtilityCraft Workbench and enter the Machinery Era. 05 Generate Dorios Energy, power machines, and automate your production lines. Increase throughput before automation by expanding the Sieve setup and choosing the right efficiency tradeoff. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 Scale up Sieving Place Sieves next to one another to grow from a single Sieve into a 3×3 and finally a 5×5 array. Up to 25 Sieves can work together. A larger array processes stacks of Gravel, Dirt, or Sand much faster. Collect extra Gravel early so you can craft the next Flint Mesh tier. 02 Upgrade Meshes Higher-tier Meshes improve eligible drops and output multipliers. Upgrade as the world expands so rare resources do not become a bottleneck. 01 Linha 02 Flint 03 Cobre 04 Ferro 05 Gold 06 Esmeralda 07 Diamante 08 Netherite 03 Process compressed resources Compress Cobblestone, Gravel, Dirt, or Sand for bulk handling. Hammers reduce compressed blocks through the same material sequence. The Sieve accepts compressed blocks and processes them faster, but the in-game guide notes an output of roughly 50% compared with normal blocks. Use this when speed matters more than efficiency. Turn renewable early resources into Steel, unlock the Workbench, and prepare the materials needed for powered production. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 Produza aço com a Forja Primitiva Siga o tutorial da Forja Primitiva para combinar pó de ferro com carbono e depois fundir o aço bruto em barras de aço. O método com SmeltFlare abaixo é outra forma de obter aço. Monte uma Forja Primitiva e produza aço.→ 02 1. Craft the SmeltFlare The SmeltFlare combines raw materials directly in your inventory. Obtain Paper by sieving Dirt for Sugar Cane, then craft the Sugar Cane into Paper. 03 2. Create Brute Steel Keep a SmeltFlare, Raw Iron, and Coal together in your inventory to form Brute Steel. Smelt Brute Steel in a Furnace or use another SmeltFlare to produce Steel Ingots. You can combine nine Brute Steel into a block and smelt the full batch at once. 04 3. Craft the Workbench Every UtilityCraft Machine, Generator, and machine Upgrade is crafted inside the Workbench. Keep Steel, Iron, Copper, Redstone, and Coal stocked for the next stage. 05 4. Power your first system 01 Craft an early generator, such as the Basic Furnator. 02 Connect or place a powered Machine in the Dorios Energy network. 03 Buffer excess power in a Battery. 04 Add Speed or Energy upgrades only after generation is stable. Every generator family has four progression tiers. Choose fuel and placement around the production line you want to sustain. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 Generator families Furnator Burns solid fuel into Energy and is the simplest early generator. Nível 1 40 DE/t Nível 2 160 DE/t Nível 3 640 DE/t Nível 4 4000 DE/t Magmator Turns Lava into Energy and pairs naturally with Crucibles and fluid transport. Nível 1 50 DE/t Nível 2 200 DE/t Nível 3 800 DE/t Nível 4 5000 DE/t Solar Panel Produces passive, fuel-free Energy when it has clear access to sunlight. Nível 1 12 DE/t Nível 2 48 DE/t Nível 3 192 DE/t Nível 4 1200 DE/t Thermo Generator Produces steady Energy from heat sources without consuming item fuel. Nível 1 20 DE/t Nível 2 80 DE/t Nível 3 320 DE/t Nível 4 2000 DE/t Wind Turbine Generates passive Energy in open areas where placement conditions are met. Nível 1 8 DE/t Nível 2 32 DE/t Nível 3 128 DE/t Nível 4 800 DE/t 02 Store excess Energy Batteries keep machines working when generation slows. Their Tier 1–4 capacities are 256k, 1.024M, 4.096M, and 25.6M DE. Anterior← MáquinasPróximo passoDrop Tables →

Secure the basic tools that turn ordinary blocks into a renewable resource loop. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 1. Craft a Hammer Save at least one log from your first tree. Use planks, logs, and sticks to craft a Wooden Hammer; upgrade to Stone when you can. While holding the Hammer, sneak and interact with Dirt or Grass to find pebbles and loose materials. Combine four matching pebbles to rebuild their full block. Special find Quantidade Source block Chance Sand Handful 1 Dirt / Grass 20% Mud Ball 1 Mud 50% Red Sand Handful 1 Red Sand / Terracotta 50% 02 2. Make a Flint Knife Use a Flint Knife to break Leaves and collect Fiber. Craft Fiber into String for your first Mesh. If Flint is scarce, combine three Gravel to craft one. Without String, the Sieve cannot be used. 03 3. Build the Sieve loop Craft a Sieve and a String Mesh, place the mesh inside, then process Gravel, Dirt, or Sand. Better meshes later unlock stronger drops and multipliers. Use the Hammer to reduce blocks in order: Cobblestone → Gravel → Dirt → Sand. Combine hammering with sieving for a fully renewable early-game loop. 01 Break Cobblestone into Gravel. 02 Sieve Gravel for ore chunks, Lapis, and gem shards. 03 Break Gravel into Dirt and sieve it for seeds and saplings. 04 Break Dirt into Sand and sieve it for Redstone and other resources. 04 4. Check your foundation Before moving on, keep a Hammer, a Flint Knife, and a Sieve fitted with a String Mesh. You should now have renewable String, Gravel, Dirt, Sand, ores, and seeds. Most UtilityCraft machines consume Dorios Energy, can output toward a configured side, and accept upgrades for speed or efficiency. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 Machine directory Assembler Repeats a crafting pattern stored on a Blueprint made by the Digitizer. Accepts Speed and Energy upgrades. Peneira Automática Processes sieveable blocks with a Mesh. Better Meshes unlock stronger drops and multipliers. Autofisher Generates fishing loot with Fishing Nets. Better Nets improve rolls, luck, and rare drops. Block Breaker Uses an installed Pickaxe to break the block directly in front of it. Block Placer Places inventory blocks into the space ahead; pair it with a Block Breaker for loops. Triturador Turns ores into dust and applies specialized yields to mineral resources. Digitizer Records crafting layouts on Blueprint Paper for use in an Assembler. Prensa Elétrica Automates plates, compression, ore reconstruction, and complete-gem assembly. Harvester Harvests mature crops and resets growth. Range upgrades expand the work area. Incinerador Smelts valid inputs with Dorios Energy instead of furnace fuel. Induction Anvil Repairs tools, armor, and other durable items using Energy. Infusor Combines an input with a catalyst to create infused materials and components. Magmatic Chamber Handles heat and lava processing with both item and liquid support. Seed Synthesizer Creates special seeds through high-energy powered synthesis. ProjetosUtilityCraftUtilityCraft Wiki Pesquisar nesta seção da wikiCtrl K Primitive Forge Pesquisar nesta seção da wikiCtrl KNavegar UtilityCraft Visão geral Visão geral Como jogar IntroductionGetting StartedExpanding ResourcesWater & LavaPrimitive ForgeFirst Steps to SteelMachinesGeneratorsDrop Tables Conteúdo ItensBlocos Sistemas MáquinasGeradores Referência ReceitasMecânicas Repositório no GitHub Metalurgia inicial · Combustível sólido Passo 05 de 09 Monte uma Forja Primitiva e produza aço. Monte oito blocos da forja, adicione combustível sólido e use os dois slots de ingredientes para fundir materiais ou combinar pó de ferro com carbono. Dispensa gerador. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 1. Fabrique oito blocos da forja Use uma bancada de trabalho comum. Cada fabricação rende quatro blocos de Forja Primitiva; repita duas vezes para montar a estrutura completa. 01 Linha superior: Tijolo · Bola de argila · Tijolo. 02 Linha central: Bola de argila · vazio · Bola de argila. 03 Linha inferior: Tijolo · Laje de tijolos de lama · Tijolo. Ingrediente Por fabricação Forja completa Tijolo 4 8 Bola de argila 3 6 Laje de tijolos de lama 1 2 Abrir a receita de fabricação da forja→ 02 2. Monte a estrutura 2×2×2 01 Coloque quatro blocos de Forja Primitiva em um quadrado 2×2. 02 Coloque mais quatro blocos diretamente sobre eles para preencher uma segunda camada 2×2. Não deixe espaços vazios. 03 A estrutura se forma automaticamente ao colocar o último bloco. A frente segue a orientação desse bloco. Interaja com a frente para abrir a forja. 03 3. Adicione ingredientes e combustível A interface possui dois slots de ingredientes, um slot separado para combustível sólido, uma seta de progresso, um indicador de combustível e quatro slots de saída em grade 2×2. Comece com carvão ou carvão vegetal no slot de combustível. Troncos, tábuas, gravetos e outros combustíveis sólidos registrados também funcionam. A forja só queima combustível durante o processamento; o tempo restante fica guardado enquanto estiver parada. O carbono no slot de ingredientes faz parte da receita do aço. Coloque combustível adicional no slot de combustível. 04 4. Funda materiais comuns Coloque um ingrediente fundível compatível em qualquer entrada. Com duas entradas compatíveis e sem receita combinada, ambas podem fundir no mesmo ciclo. Cada entrada processa uma receita por ciclo. Um ciclo comum leva 40 ticks (2 segundos a 20 ticks/s); uma pilha no slot alimenta os próximos ciclos. Os quatro slots de saída servem para armazenamento e não aumentam o número de receitas por entrada. Entrada Result Ciclo 1 Pó de ferro 1 Barra de ferro 40 ticks · 2 s 1 Aço bruto 1 Barra de aço 40 ticks · 2 s 05 5. Produza aço bruto e depois barras de aço Antes de preparar a liga, minere minério de ferro ou minério de ferro de ardósia com um martelo compatível para obter pó de ferro. Um Triturador energizado também pode produzi-lo mais adiante. Use pó de ferro na combinação; ferro bruto e barras de ferro não o substituem nesta receita da forja. 01 Coloque pó de ferro em um slot de ingredientes. 02 Coloque carvão, carvão vegetal, pó de carvão ou pó de carvão vegetal no outro. A ordem dos ingredientes pode ser invertida. 03 Forneça combustível sólido separado e mantenha espaço livre na saída. A receita combinada tem prioridade sobre a fundição comum. 04 Após 160 ticks (8 segundos a 20 ticks/s), colete um aço bruto para cada unidade de pó de ferro e de carbono consumida. 05 Retire o ingrediente de carbono e coloque o aço bruto em qualquer entrada. Funda por 40 ticks para obter uma barra de aço. Ver todas as receitas da Forja Primitiva→Ver receitas de pó de ferro→ 06 6. Mantenha a forja funcionando Se o processamento parar, confira a montagem dos oito blocos, os ingredientes da receita, a disponibilidade de combustível e o espaço na saída. Um ciclo em andamento pausa se os resultados não couberem. Mudar a receita ou retirar ingredientes reservados para o ciclo atual reinicia o progresso. Quebrar um bloco da forja desmonta a estrutura e derruba os ingredientes, os itens de combustível e os produtos armazenados. Esvazie antes de mover. Ver especificações da forja→Avançar para a Era das Máquinas→ Anterior← Water & LavaPróximo passoFirst Steps to Steel →

These fluid loops unlock early automation, farming, Nether access, and the path to your first generator. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Geradores09Drop Tables 01 1. Obtain Water 01 Craft a Mortar with three Cobblestone and one Stone Pebble. 02 Combine the Mortar, one Glass Bottle, and two Saplings to make a Water Bottle. The Mortar is not consumed. 03 Use three Water Bottles on a Cauldron, then collect the water with a Bucket. 02 2. Craft the Crucible The Crucible requires four Bricks and four Mud Bricks. Smelt Clay for Bricks; Clay comes from sieving Sand. Use a Water Bottle on placed Dirt to create Mud, combine Mud with Wheat for Packed Mud, then craft four Packed Mud into one Mud Brick. 03 3. Produce Lava Place the Crucible above a heat source and insert four Cobblestone to slowly produce one bucket of Lava. Stronger heat sources finish faster. Heat source Heat value Lava / Flowing Lava 4 Soul Fire / Soul Torch / Soul Campfire 4 Fire / Campfire / Magma Block 3 Torch 1 04 4. Make Obsidian Interact with a Crucible using a Water Bucket to create Obsidian instantly. Stable Water and Lava production now gives you the foundation for energy generation.
